title: Two outputs from one value
starter:
# x: 4 floats in slot 0. Write x * x into slot 1 (4 floats) and the sum of x * x into slot 2 (1 float).
# Stage x * x so both outputs read one materialized copy. This starter writes only slot 1.
%x  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=0
%y  = buffer 4 dtype=f32 slot=1
%z  = buffer 1 dtype=f32 slot=2
%v  = load %x
%sq = mul %v %v
%sy = store %y %sq
%y1 = after %y %sy
hints: Slot 2 needs a `reduce op=add` of the squares, stored through a `shape=[]` view of the 1-element buffer.
Put `%q = stage %sq` between the square and its two uses, and use `%q` in both the store into slot 1 and the reduce. Each output still needs its own `store` and `after`.
Two buffers, two version chains: `after %y %sy` and `after %z %sz` are independent. Nothing orders them against each other, and nothing needs to.
explain: One value, two consumers: the store into slot 1 and the reduce into slot 2. With `stage`, rangeify computes the squares once into a temp buffer and both loops read it. Without it, each loop would recompute `x * x`. The results are the same bits either way.
